description: Protocol message vectors (RFC-0036, schema version 1, tessera-protocol/1), written by generate.py, an oracle independent of the Rust crates and the Python package. Each `messages` entry decodes from `payload` as `type` under `limits` to `value` (README.md 'Values'), encodes back to `payload`, and every proper prefix of `payload` fails with ERR-CODEC-TRUNCATED at the offset `truncated` gives: runs [length, offset], each covering the prefixes from its length to the next run's; `envelope` is its RFC-0003 envelope at schema version 1, which a reader of the schema opens to `value`. A Round1's `statement_digest` is H("statement", TCE(statement)). Each `coin_toss` entry gives commitment = H("coin-commit", s_V) and seed = H("coin-toss", s_V || s_P). Decoding a `refused` entry as `type`, under its own `limits` if it has them, fails with `code` at `offset`, the first byte the failing check reads (RFC-0003 'Limits'); an `accepted` entry sits exactly at its limits and decodes. Opening an `envelopes` entry as a message of `schema` fails with `code` at `offset`, counted from the envelope's start.
